SMTO-GML-0073 — SMTO couldn't find that email conversation

GUID: 9d6e98d8-4ebb-57c4-9780-c437d8777d96
Slug: gmail-imap-thread-missing
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail-imap

What happened

  • SMTO searched the folders it can see in this Gmail account, including Spam and Trash, and found no emails in that conversation. It may have been deleted, or it belongs to a different account.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Gmail and check that the conversation still exists and hasn't been permanently deleted or emptied from Trash. SMTO already searched Spam and Trash too, so a missing conversation is the most likely reason.
  2. Make sure you asked SMTO to use the right Gmail account, especially if more than one account is set up. A conversation from one account can't be found in another account's mailbox.
  3. Ask SMTO to search for the conversation again, for example by sender or subject, then ask it to act on the one it finds. A fresh search gives SMTO the conversation's current details instead of an old reference.
  4. If this was part of a larger request, read SMTO's result for the other steps before asking for the whole thing again. Other emails in the same request may already have been changed.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the conversation in its new search and the action on it completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with the account and the conversation's sender and subject. Don't repeat a change SMTO reported as uncertain until you've checked it in Gmail.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's IMAP mailbox (gateway_core/gmail_imap.Mailbox.thread_ids) searched All Mail, Drafts, Spam and Trash for the X-GM-THRID and found no messages, raising gmail_thread_not_found (catalogued as gmail_imap_thread_missing).

What this means

  • No messages belonging to the selected thread were found in the observed IMAP folders. Existing execution and mutation uncertainty remain authoritative; response prose cannot supply a missing cause.

Why this can happen

  • No message IDs for the selected thread appear in the observed folders.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained operation, condition and effect evidence before choosing a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the mailbox listing (search or list messages) for the intended app-password account and use a current thread ID from it; a thread ID from another account or a permanently deleted thread returns no X-GM-THRID matches. Mailbox.thread_ids searches only the All Mail, Drafts, Spam and Trash folders the IMAP server exposes, so also confirm those labels have Show in IMAP enabled in Gmail. If this lookup was part of a larger action, check the operation's recorded results before repeating any write whose effect is unknown.
  • Refresh the mailbox listing and select a current thread ID in the intended account.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first; existing effect evidence and replay checks still decide whether a new attempt is permitted.

How to verify the fix

  • The reported prerequisite is satisfied and a new authorized operation returns its actual result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a write whose external effect is still unknown.

Technical notes

  • Diagnostic presentation does not start recovery or alter authorization.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
